hypothesis: If the permanent spiral forms of organisms (ruminant horns, molluscan and foraminiferal shells, sunflower capitula) are logarithmic spirals, then for any such structure the linear size of the growing edge (radius vector or whorl size) must increase exponentially with angle of rotation about the spiral's pole, r = a e^(b theta), and must do so better than the alternative simple spirals (Archimedean r = a + b theta, which grows linearly; Fermat / parabolic r = a sqrt(theta + theta0), which decelerates).
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Only the molluscan-shell class can be tested with public data located (see interpretation). For every gastropod specimen in Collins et al. 2021 with >= 5 digitised successive half-whorl apertures, take the square root of aperture area as the linear whorl size at angles 0, pi, 2 pi, ...; for every ammonoid species in Korn & Walton 2018 with >= 5 half-whorl diameters, take conch diameter at each half whorl. Fit the three two-parameter models by least squares in the size domain and compare root-mean-square residuals. The claim (for molluscan shells) is supported if the logarithmic model has the lowest RMSE in >= 80% of gastropod specimens and in >= 80% of ammonoid species, and the median ratio RMSE(Archimedean) / RMSE(logarithmic) exceeds 1.5 in both groups. Because horns, foraminifera and sunflower capitula remain untested, the confidence attached to a supporting verdict is capped at 0.5.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. The claim is refuted (for molluscan shells, and hence as a universal) if the logarithmic model is best in fewer than 50% of specimens in either group, or if the median RMSE ratio Archimedean / logarithmic is below 1.0 in either group. Intermediate results are 'mixed'.
interpretation: Thompson's statement is a universal over four classes of structure plus a stated exception (the cordate leaf). Public coordinate data were found only for molluscan shells: no digitised floret positions of sunflower capitula (the Swinton et al. 2016 citizen-science deposit gives parastichy counts and annotated photographs, not coordinates), no horn centre-line or outline data, and no foraminiferal chamber-position tables were located on Dryad, Zenodo or figshare; MorphoSource meshes require a login. The test therefore covers only the molluscan class, and its verdict is explicitly a test of that class with the caveat that a logarithmic fit for molluscs cannot establish the universal. 'Logarithmic spiral' is operationalized as exponential growth of linear whorl size with rotation angle: in a gastropod, the square root of aperture area at successive half whorls; in an ammonoid, conch diameter at successive half whorls (for a planispiral conch the diameter is the sum of two opposite radius vectors and grows exponentially if and only if the radius does). Both datasets were already downloaded for claim tests thompson1917-ch11-05 and thompson1917-ch11-15; those tests examined allometry of conch proportions and whorl-expansion and apical angles, not the comparison of spiral models made here.
